title: a captain's A on a merge card survives a main-only move: when main moved after the card was raised, fm-merge waits for the autopilot's branch update, CI and gates on the new head, and merges that head under the same answer when the review, patch and inputs are unchanged; any other change still refuses and says why
acceptance: Why. Three times on 2026-10-05 the captain chose A on a merge card and nothing merged, because another PR merged into main between the card and the click (T-216, T-214, T-218). Evidence for T-218: card D-firstmate-workflow-T218-2 was raised on head a0ed76a with readiness gate_base 601aaad; T-215 (#206) merged at 14:25:29Z; the captain answered A at 14:27:09Z; the board recorded `merge failed: fm-merge: candidate lacks current signed readiness / 候選版本缺少有效的已簽署就緒證據` (events.jsonl, decision_made at 14:27:20Z). The PR was then BEHIND; firstmate had to update the branch, wait for CI, rerun the six gates and raise a fresh card, and the captain had to click again. Nothing about the task's change, its review or its inputs differed. These dated card/event observations are supplied operational evidence from the retained session history; they are not asserted to exist in the isolated implementation-review checkout.

Mechanism (root cause). bin/fm-merge.sh:92 refuses when the PR head differs from `--expected-head`, and bin/fm-merge.sh:138 refuses when `fm_binding candidate --head <expected>` fails. `candidate` (bin/lib/fm_binding.py:365-387) requires the signed readiness record's `gate_base` to equal the live base tip (:377) and calls `verify_current` (:386, :316-323), so any move of main voids the card's readiness even when the head is unchanged. Under strict branch protection the PR then becomes BEHIND, the autopilot updates the branch (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py:142-179, design §15.8 'Branch updates'), CI and the gates run on the new head, and gate 6 already carries the same signed review across a base-only update when the stable patch-id and file list are unchanged (fm_binding.py `ready` :416-424; design §15.8 'Gate 6 decides whether an approval carries'). One step is still manual today: every gate and readiness on the updated head calls `verified_base` (bin/lib/fm_binding.py:289-301), which refuses 'local base is stale; synchronize before accepting' until the local base ref matches the live tip, and nothing automated moves the local base (the autopilot fast-forwards only task refs, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py:61-140; `prepare_head`, bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:122-140, fetches without moving; `fm_external_base`, bin/fm-config.sh:1066-1080, runs only from fm-worker.sh:83 and fm-review.sh:85; design.md:5861 makes it a firstmate step). Change 5 makes the carry wait do that sync, so a fresh signed readiness for the new head that cites the same review then arrives without any human step; today only the captain's answer is lost, because fm-merge knows only the old head.

Change 1, a shared candidate check (bin/lib/fm_binding.py). Move the body of the `candidate` branch of main() (:365-387) into a function `candidate(root, repo, task, pr, head)` that returns the readiness record or raises ValueError with the same messages as today. The function itself first repeats the live-head check that main() does at :359-360 ('authoritative PR head moved; candidate is stale') and opens the Store as :361-362 do, so it is complete on its own; main()'s `candidate` mode calls it and prints the JSON exactly as before. No behaviour of the `candidate` mode changes. The function looks up `remote_head`, `view_base`, `git`, `command`, `source_binding`, `required_checks` and `selected_review` through module globals at call time (no default-argument binding, no local aliases), because tests/external-reviews.test.sh:197-218 runs `fm_binding.main()` in `candidate` mode while patching those module-level names and must keep passing unchanged. Callers of the `candidate` mode, all unchanged: tests/external-reviews.test.sh:197-218, bin/fm-merge.sh:138, bin/fm-decide.sh:438 and :484, tests/lib/evidence_binding.py:130 and :150, the fixture in tests/lib/binding-fixture.sh (modes tuple :18, `candidate` :47-49). The shared candidate function itself loads mapping = gate_list(). Move the authorized-adoption guard currently at fm_binding.py:338-348 into a shared validation helper: call it from candidate() and the ordinary guarded main modes, avoiding duplicate validation for candidate. candidate() must still validate the PR matches the authorized adoption, base_matches and sync_base before accepting readiness; carry reaches this same guard. Add signed authorized and unauthorized adopted-PR carry cases, proving the guard cannot be bypassed.

Change 2, a new `carry` mode (bin/lib/fm_binding.py). `fm_binding.py carry --task T --pr N --head <H0 the card's head> --bound-signature <the card's readiness record signature>`; add 'carry' to the `mode` choices (:329) and an argument `--bound-signature` (default ''). main() dispatches `carry` BEFORE the shared live-head check at :359-360 (that check is exactly the case carry exists for), to a function `carry(root, repo, task, pr, h0, bound)` that opens the Store itself. `carry` does not use the shared error handler at :434-440 (except at :437). The function raises one of two exception classes defined in fm_binding.py, `CarryRefused(ValueError)` (lasting) or `CarryWaiting(ValueError)` (not yet), and main() maps them to exit 1 or 75, printing one line 'fm-binding: <english reason>' on stderr either way; any other exception raised inside `carry` is wrapped as `CarryWaiting` except where named below. Steps: (0) review policy: when `review_policy()` (:248) is 'external' or 'both' and the PR head differs from H0, refuse (exit 1) 'external review policy: a review identity is bound to its head, so an answer does not carry across a head change; a new card is needed' (an external review's identity hashes the PR head, bin/lib/fm_external.py:185-188, so it can never match after a branch update); the same-head case still runs the steps below. (a) read the Store's signed records (Store.records() verifies every signature) and select the readiness record R0 whose `signature` equals `--bound-signature`, whose `head` is H0, whose `pr` is N and whose `repository` is the PR's repository; none is exit 1 'card readiness record not found'. A Store integrity error ('forged or modified local evidence record', bin/lib/fm_evidence.py:173-176, or any ValueError raised by Store.records()) is exit 1 'evidence store failed verification: <reason>', never a wait. (b) read the authoritative PR with `remote_head`, plus `mergeStateStatus` through `github(repo, 'pr', 'view', N, '--repo', repo, '--json', 'mergeStateStatus')`; a PR that is not open is exit 1. (c) fetch `refs/pull/<N>/head` with `fetch_ref`; require H1 (the PR head) == the fetched SHA (else 75: the head is moving); then, with the objects present, require H0 an ancestor of H1 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, run with subprocess directly and its exit code read - not through `command()`, which turns every non-zero exit into 'binding command failed' - so exit 1 means 'not an ancestor' and other codes are errors) and `git rev-list --no-merges H1 ^H0 ^<live base tip>` empty, so the only commits added since the card are merges of the base; otherwise exit 1 'the PR head gained its own commits since the card; a new card is needed'. A missing H0 object after a successful fetch is exit 1. The live base tip comes from `verified_base`; its 'local base is stale; synchronize before accepting' is 75 (main moved and the operator's local base is not yet fast-forwarded). (d) lasting refusals on H1, each exit 1 with its reason, checked before waiting for readiness: the latest signed verdict for the task (the same `selected_review` that `candidate` uses) is not an APPROVE ('no current local approval'), or its `review_identity` differs from R0['verdict_signature'], or the external signature differs from R0.get('external_signature') ('the review changed since the card'); `source_binding` for H1 against `merge-base(<live base>, H1)` differs from R0['review']['binding'] in any of 'patch', 'files', 'spec_sha256', 'contract_sha256', 'conventions_sha256' ('the task change differs from the card: <key>'); `required_checks(root, repo, pr, H1)` raising a reason that contains exactly 'required check/status failed' (fm_binding.py:227) ('a required check failed on <H1 short>'). (e) same head: candidate success is accepted subject to step (g). On candidate failure, apply classification precedence: explicitly lasting evidence/source/review/refused-adoption and failed-required-check conditions from (a)-(d) refuse first. A known same-head DIRTY conflict refuses immediately with '<candidate reason>; the branch will not be updated (DIRTY); a new card is needed', including external DIRTY-and-behind, because the autopilot cannot update a conflicted PR. Transient Git/GitHub reads, pending/unknown/stale check reads, moving heads and external-review-not-ready remain CarryWaiting (75), even on CLEAN/BLOCKED/UNSTABLE/HAS_HOOKS; mergeStateStatus must never turn them into permanent errors. For the remaining readiness invalidation that requires branch update (no signed readiness, gate-base moved or required-check evidence needing refresh), BEHIND or UNKNOWN waits; for external projects, non-conflicted fresh ancestry-behind also waits even if CLEAN. When caught up and status CLEAN/BLOCKED/UNSTABLE/HAS_HOOKS, that readiness invalidation refuses '<candidate reason>; the branch will not be updated (<mergeStateStatus>); a new card is needed', because no unchanged-head regate will arrive while landed() matches the running answer. (f) then call `candidate(root, repo, task, pr, H1)`: success gives R1; a raise is exit 75 with its reason. (g) on success also require R1['verdict_signature'] == R0['verdict_signature'] (exit 1 otherwise), and print R1 as JSON with an added field `carried_from: H0`. Classification rule: every reason named above as exit 1 is lasting (including the review-policy and Store-integrity refusals); every other error (including 'no signed six-gate readiness for candidate', 'candidate gate base moved; refresh gates', 'required check/status pending', 'PR head/base moved while reading checks', 'checks belong to stale head', 'required checks unknown: …', 'external review not ready: …', and a `binding command failed: …` from a transient git or gh call) is exit 75, so a transient failure waits and the fm-merge deadline bounds it. For FM_EXTERNAL=1, decide whether the branch awaits update from fresh ancestry as the autopilot does, rather than mergeStateStatus alone: fetch the live base and PR head into private refs using fetch_ref; verify fetched PR head equals the observed head; git merge-base --is-ancestor <base> <head> exit 1 means behind and CarryWaiting only after the explicit lasting refusals and known same-head DIRTY conflict have been checked, exit 0 means caught up, other exits mean unverifiable and CarryWaiting. Keep the existing lasting refusal for a changed external-review head. Test an unprotected same-head external PR whose mergeStateStatus is CLEAN but ancestry is behind. Pre-sync validation interface: add a --pre-sync boolean argument to carry mode. With --pre-sync, carry validates the bound signed readiness record/Store integrity, authoritative OPEN state and head, changed external-policy head refusal, current local review identity (including superseding REJECT or newer APPROVE), adopted-PR authorization and known same-head DIRTY conflict, before any successful base synchronization is required. It performs no base sync and no readiness acceptance or merge; on validation success it prints an explicit precheck JSON object (not a readiness record) and exits 0. These validations are shared with full carry, which repeats them and checks all base-dependent ancestry/source/check/readiness conditions after sync; no cached precheck result grants eligibility. A known lasting refusal is exit1 immediately; unreadable/transient validation is exit75 with its reason. No speculative refusal is inferred from missing remote evidence. The no-flag carry interface and exception handling remain as specified.

Change 3, fm-merge waits for the carried readiness (bin/fm-merge.sh). New optional argument `--bound-signature <sig>`, parsed like the others with `fm_need "fm-merge" "$@"` before its `shift 2` (bin/ci.sh's option-loop lint and tests/option-loop.test.sh:141-145 require it), validated as 64 lowercase hex, else exit 64. The carry path needs a task: it runs only when `--task` is given (the board always passes it for tracked cards, board/server.ts:1946-1947); with `--bound-signature` and no `--task`, the flag is ignored and today's path runs. Today's path is unchanged when the PR head equals `--expected-head` and `fm_binding candidate` passes. Otherwise, when `--bound-signature` is given and the card is a task's (not `--untracked`): instead of refusing at :92 or :131, loop until a deadline of `${FM_MERGE_CARRY_SECONDS:-3600}` seconds, sleeping `${FM_MERGE_CARRY_POLL:-30}` seconds between tries: re-read the PR (`state`, `headRefName`, `title`, `headRefOid`, `baseRefName`) and run the task/branch ownership checks (:94-123) against that view FIRST, refusing as they do today; then, when `baseRefName` is not the project's base (`main` for the self project, `$FM_BASE` for an external one), refuse at once (exit 1) 'fm-merge: the captain's answer carries only for a pull request on the project base, not one stacked on <baseRefName> / 船長的答案只能沿用到以專案主分支為基底的 PR，這個 PR 疊在 <baseRefName> 上', so a stacked card never holds the merge turn; only then does MERGED print the existing 'already merged' line and exit 0 (the order :99-104 explains: ownership is checked before 'already merged' can settle the wrong card); any other non-OPEN state refuses as today; before Change5 synchronization, run `fm_binding carry --pre-sync --task "${TASK}" --pr "${PR}" --head "${EXPECTED_HEAD}" --bound-signature "${BOUND}"`; exit1 refuses immediately using the carry refusal translations, exit75 waits with its last reason, and exit0 permits synchronization. After sync0 only, run the full `fm_binding carry --task "$TASK" --pr "$PR" --head "$EXPECTED_HEAD" --bound-signature "$BOUND"`. Exit 0: take H1 from the JSON `head`, re-run the ownership checks against a fresh view if the view is older than this try, then merge with `--match-head-commit H1` (not EXPECTED_HEAD) and continue to the emit and cleanup exactly as today, with the merged event's `--data` set to `{"carried_from":"<H0>","head":"<H1>"}` and the summary lines 'merged #N from the board (carried from <H0 short> to <H1 short>)' / '從看板合併 #N（答案沿用：<H0 short> → <H1 short>）'. Exit 75: keep the last reason and try again. Exit 1 (or any other non-zero): refuse at once with 'fm-merge: the captain's answer cannot carry to the current head: <reason> / 船長的答案無法沿用到目前版本：<reason>' and exit 1. Deadline reached: refuse with 'fm-merge: waited <minutes> min for readiness on the updated head: <last reason> / 已等待 <minutes> 分鐘，更新後的版本仍未就緒：<last reason>' and exit 1. Without `--bound-signature` (older cards, untracked cards) the refusals at :92 and :131 stay exactly as they are. fm-merge never updates the PR branch, never reruns CI and never runs a gate itself: the autopilot owns those (design §15.8). Its one write during the wait is the local base fast-forward of Change 5. Brace every variable in the zh-TW strings (bash 3.2 reads CJK bytes after a bare $name as part of the name). Code root during the wait: for the self project the sync of Change 5 fast-forwards the same checkout fm-merge runs from, and bash reads a script as it runs (skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:606). So before its first carry try fm-merge copies its own `bin/` directory (`cp -R "$_fm_code_dir"` into a `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-merge-carry.XXXXXX"` directory, removed on exit) and re-execs the copy's fm-merge.sh with the same arguments and an internal marker `FM_MERGE_CARRY_CODE=<copy>` so the copy does not copy again; the re-exec explicitly exports FM_CODE_ROOT as the copied engine parent (the directory containing copied bin), while preserving the real FM_ROOT, FM_TARGET_ROOT, FM_STATE_DIR, FM_EVIDENCE_PROJECT and other storage/project roots. FM_MERGE_CARRY_CODE only prevents recursive copying; it is not a replacement for FM_CODE_ROOT. All downstream code resolution uses that copied FM_CODE_ROOT, including adoption ownership (fm-merge.sh:100), project initialization (fm-config.sh:1058), binding wrappers, emission and cleanup (fm-cleanup.sh:66). The copy runs `fm_binding`, `fm-emit.sh` and `fm-cleanup.sh` from the copied `bin/` while `--repo`/`REPO` still names the real checkout for state and git. One code root therefore serves the whole wait; §15.8 says so. Use the explicit mktemp template above, never bare mktemp -d. The claimed SKILL.md:606 source is withdrawn: immutable engine code is required directly by this acceptance. Compose one EXIT cleanup function for the copied engine directory and all Change 5 temporary/private refs; neither helper replaces the other EXIT trap. Preserve exit status and retain unknown resources safely. Cleanup emitter correction (scope proposal): bin/fm-cleanup.sh:119 currently executes "$REPO/bin/fm-emit.sh". Resolve that executable from "${FM_CODE_ROOT:-$REPO}/bin/fm-emit.sh", consistently with its existing code-root lookup at :66, while keeping --repo and every project/state/evidence/git root pointed at the real checkout. With FM_CODE_ROOT unset, existing cleanup behavior is unchanged. This is the sole newly scoped production file; it makes the already-required immutable code chain complete.

Change 4, the board hands the bound signature (board/server.ts). `startMerge` (:1937) gains a `boundSignature` parameter; the answer handler (:2734) passes `p.binding?.signature` when it is a string matching /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/, else "". `startMerge` adds `--bound-signature <sig>` to the fm-merge argv only when it is non-empty and the card is not untracked. So a fixture card whose binding signature is not 64 hex (tests/lib/binding-fixture.sh:49 writes 'fixture') forwards nothing and keeps today's path. The decision record keeps `expected_head` and `binding` as the card had them (:2665). `mergeFailureTw` (:1894-1903) gains two mappings placed FIRST, before every existing one: a reason containing 'cannot carry to the current head' -> '船長的答案無法沿用到目前版本；需要新的合併卡', and one containing 'for readiness on the updated head' -> '等待更新後版本就緒逾時；需要新的合併卡'. While fm-merge waits, the decision record stays merge 'running' and the project's merge marker stays held, so no other merge in that project can move main again during the wait; this is intended and the design says so. A board restart during the wait leaves the running helper alone while its marker's pid is alive (:1872-1876). The autopilot keeps working during the wait: `landed()` (bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:50-55) matches only `expected_head == head`, so after the branch update the PR's new head is advanced and gated as usual (`advance` uses `merge_blocker` only in its fingerprint, :303-315), and `merge_card` (:490-495) raises no second card because a running merge blocks it (:490-495) and the task's decision record exists (:491-495).

Change 5, the carry wait synchronizes the local base (new file bin/lib/fm-carry-base.sh, sourced by bin/fm-merge.sh right after bin/lib/fm-stack.sh (:36-37), behind the same kind of guard as :32-33: a missing file prints 'fm-merge: missing <path>' and exits 70; the file starts with `# shellcheck shell=bash` and `# fm:sourced` like bin/lib/fm-stack.sh). It defines `fm_carry_sync_base <base-name>` and fm-merge calls it on every carry try after the successful independent pre-sync validation specified in Changes2/3 and before full `fm_binding carry`, with the PR's `baseRefName` from that try's re-read view (Change 3); it never runs outside the carry path. An empty or missing `baseRefName` returns 75 'the PR base name is unreadable' (never a silent skip). It is called only with the project's base (Change 3 refuses a stacked PR before any sync); a different name returns 75 'not the project base' as a guard. Self project (FM_EXTERNAL != 1, root = the engine checkout `$FM_TARGET_ROOT`): fetch into a private ref the same way `fetch_ref` does (bin/lib/fm_binding.py:36-46), so no concurrent fetch can change what is read: `git -C <root> fetch -q --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head "$(git -C <root> remote get-url origin)" "+refs/heads/<base>:refs/fm/carry-base/<pid>-<random>"`, read R from that ref with `rev-parse`, and delete the private ref on every exit path (a trap or an explicit cleanup); fetching by URL with an explicit destination writes no FETCH_HEAD and no remote-tracking ref. FETCH_HEAD is never read. A failed fetch returns 75 'cannot fetch the live base'. Let L = `refs/heads/<base>`. A missing L (no such branch, or an unborn checked-out branch) returns 75 'the local base ref <base> does not exist'; nothing is created. L == R returns 0. L not an ancestor of R returns 75 'the local base has commits the live base lacks; it cannot be fast-forwarded'. Otherwise: when `<base>` is checked out in a linked worktree other than <root> (look it up in `git -C <root> worktree list --porcelain`, as bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py:99-111 does), return 75 'the local base is checked out in another worktree <path>; synchronize it there' and move nothing. When `<base>` is the branch checked out in <root>, run `git -C <root> merge -q --ff-only R`: git's own fast-forward, which leaves unrelated modified and untracked files in place and refuses (non-zero) only if a file it must update is dirty; a refusal returns 75 'the local base cannot be fast-forwarded without touching local changes'. When `<base>` is checked out in no worktree, run `git -C <root> update-ref refs/heads/<base> R L` (compare-and-swap). Never `reset`, `checkout`, `stash` or `clean`; the only refs written are `refs/heads/<base>` and the deleted private ref (and, for an external project, `refs/remotes/origin/$FM_BASE`). External project (FM_EXTERNAL = 1): `git -C "$FM_TARGET_ROOT" fetch -q --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head origin "+refs/heads/$FM_BASE:refs/remotes/origin/$FM_BASE"` (an explicit destination: it writes only the remote-tracking ref that `fm_external_base` reads), then the existing `fm_external_base` (bin/fm-config.sh:1066-1080, unchanged); its 65 (dirty clone, other branch checked out, not a fast-forward) and a failed fetch return 75 with its reason. Since immediate independent lasting refusals are checked before synchronization on every try, a sync75 cannot hide them. A 75 from the sync keeps fm-merge waiting like a 75 from `carry` (the reason is kept as the last reason, so the deadline refusal names it: 'fm-merge: waited <minutes> min for readiness on the updated head: <reason> / 已等待 <minutes> 分鐘，更新後的版本仍未就緒：<reason>'); fm-merge prints nothing and continues to `fm_binding carry` after a 0. Because fm-merge syncs on every try (default every 30 s) from the moment the captain answers, the local base is current well before the new head's CI settles and the autopilot starts its gates, so those gates do not fail on a stale base. The sync runs only after the task/branch ownership checks of that try. Callers of `fm_external_base`, unchanged: bin/fm-worker.sh:83, bin/fm-review.sh:85; tests/external-execution.test.sh covers it today and stays unchanged.

What still refuses (unchanged or explicit), each with its reason in en and zh-TW: a PR head that gained a non-merge commit, a different patch-id or file list, a changed spec/contract/conventions hash, a superseding review (REJECT or a newer verdict), a different external review signature, a failed required check on the new head, a PR closed without merging, a conflict on an unchanged head (mergeStateStatus DIRTY: refused at once by step (e) of Change 2), a conflict or failure that appears only after the branch was updated (no readiness arrives for the new head: the deadline refusal names the last reason), the card's own readiness record missing, a Store record whose signature does not verify (refused at once, not at the deadline), and any project whose review policy is external or both when the head changed (refused at once: external review identities are head-bound). A refused carry leaves the decision record 'failed' with that reason, and firstmate raises a fresh card as today.

Tests (fail-first; workers do not run suites, CI and the gates verify). (1) a new file tests/lib/evidence_carry.py, run by tests/evidence-binding.test.sh after preserving the existing command-and-status-assertion pair (tests/evidence-binding.test.sh:34-35), then invoking the new script with its own assert_eq status check and a separate fresh temporary directory; the existing command is `python3 "$ROOT/tests/lib/evidence_binding.py" "$ROOT" "$t"` at :34, followed by its unchanged assertion at :35, so tests/lib/evidence_binding.py stays unchanged and no step order there is disturbed. It builds its own disposable repository, signed APPROVE, gh stub, gate transcript and readiness for a head H0 by the same steps evidence_binding.py uses at :13-131 (copy them; the gh stub additionally returns `mergeStateStatus` from remote.json, which its `--json` key filter already allows), records the readiness signature S0, and keeps one APPROVE as the latest verdict until its last step. Every assertion checks both the exit code and the stderr reason text. Steps, in this order: (i) same head: add a base-only commit to main (local main updated) while the PR head stays H0, then with remote.json mergeStateStatus CLEAN `carry --head H0 --bound-signature S0` exits 1 naming 'will not be updated'; DIRTY exits 1 naming 'will not be updated (DIRTY)'; BEHIND exits 75; UNKNOWN exits 75. (ii) merge main into the task branch (H1), point refs/pull/9/head and remote.json headRefOid at H1; `carry` exits 75 while no readiness for H1 exists. (iii) stale local base: make `git clone --mirror` of the repository after (ii) (so it holds main and refs/pull/9/head), point the `url.<root>.insteadOf` rewrite at that mirror, move local `main` one commit back with update-ref, assert exit 75 naming 'local base is stale', then restore local `main` and the original rewrite. (iv) write a gate transcript for H1 with HEAD and the current BASE and run `ready` for H1; `carry` exits 0 and prints head H1 with carried_from == H0. (v) an unknown `--bound-signature` (64 hex) exits 1 naming 'card readiness record not found'. (vi) red check before readiness: add a second base-only commit to main, merge it into the branch (H2), point refs and remote.json at H2, set STATUS_STATE=failure: exit 1 naming 'required check failed'; then set STATUS_STATE back to success. (vii) a non-merge commit that changes src/feature on top of H2 (refs and remote updated): exit 1 naming 'gained its own commits'. (viii) with refs back at H1: import fm_binding with FM_* env set as above, patch `fm_binding.review_policy` to return 'external', and call the `carry` function directly: it raises `CarryRefused` naming 'external review policy'; restore the patch. (ix) copy one evidence record file aside, change its `head` field in place, assert `carry` exits 1 naming 'evidence store failed verification', then restore the file. (x) last: append a signed REJECT verdict for the task; exit 1 naming 'no current local approval'. Red on base: the `carry` mode does not exist. (2) tests/lib/binding-fixture.sh: add 'carry' to the fixture's intercepted modes (:18) and `--bound-signature` (default '') to the fixture's parser (:21-25), with behaviour driven by fixture files in FM_TARGET_ROOT: `.fixture-carry` holding a JSON readiness object is printed with exit 0, `.fixture-carry-wait` exits 75 with its text on stderr, `.fixture-carry-refuse` exits 1 with its text on stderr; with none of them, exit 1 'no carry'. (3) tests/merge.test.sh, with that fixture and the existing gh stub.
